reuse.why: Every inline midpoint copy (forecast, updateActions, posting, preview, schedule template) and every client caller goes through the existing shared getScheduledAmount, and the tolerance comes from the existing getApproxNumberThreshold.

duplication.why: It removes five duplicated copies of the expected-amount rule and leaves one definition.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, and server, API model and client layers consume it.

scope.why: The edits all serve the four steps, but the step-1 release note ('furthest from zero') is left contradicting the final rule, next to a third note.

maintainability.why: There is one small, well-tested definition, and switching to an options object `{ op, inverse }` avoids positional boolean arguments while making the operator variation explicit at each call site.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No site re-implements the amount rule after the change.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts gains an `op` option (inverse moved into the same options object) and one isapprox branch, which is the real variation the steps require. Every planning and display caller passes its operator.
